subject: Unexpected z-value for fixed parameter in standardizedSolution

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Unexpected z-value for fixed parameter in standardizedSolution
parts:
On 03/23/2018 05:16 AM, Mark Seeto wrote:
> Dear Yves and lavaan group,
>
> I'm seeing what seems like strange behaviour in lavaan versions 0.5-23
> and 0.6-1.1204, but which doesn't happen with version 0.5-22.
>
> Here is one particular row of the output from standardizedSolution(),
> for the same data and the same code, for those three versions.
>
> ## lavaan 0.5-22 in R 3.3.1:
>    lhs op rhs est.std    se       z pvalue
> 36  F1 ~~  F1   1.000 0.000      NA     NA
>
> ## lavaan 0.5-23 in R 3.4.3:
>    lhs op rhs est.std    se            z pvalue
> 36  F1 ~~  F1   1.000 0.000 17957505.192  0.000
>
> ## lavaan 0.6-1.1204 in R 3.4.3:
>    lhs op rhs est.std    se            z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
> 36  F1 ~~  F1   1.000 0.000 35915010.440  0.000    1.000    1.000

Thanks for reporting this. I had a look a the example, and this is a
numerical issue.

To compute standard errors for standardized parameters, lavaan uses the
delta method, using a numerical approximation of the jacobian (relating
the unstandardized to the standardized estimates). Hence, there is some
numerical 'fuzz'.

In practice, I have to 'check' if a standard error is identified or not
by comparing it to a small constant. If it is too small, then it was
probably not identified, and you get NA. In your example, the SE for F1
~~ F1 was 2.784351e-08. The current source code (0.5-23, 0.6-1 until
now) has:

tmp < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)

and all those SEs will be set to NA. Now sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) is
(on most machines) equal to 1.490116e-08, so we just missed it...

I have now lowered the threshold and the next update (0.6-1.1212) will use

tmp < .Machine$double.eps^(1/3)

Choosing reasonable cutoff values like this is somewhat of an art.

Yves.
